title: The Observatory
story: You and NOVA are on a night visit to the observatory when the dome door locks. NOVA is learning astronomy to help the telescope find objects. Get it right to open the dome.
escaped: The dome slides open to the stars. NOVA now sorts planets, predicts the Moon's phases and knows its comets from its satellites.

locks.title: Inner or outer planet?
locks.intro: NOVA must sort planets into inner planets and outer planets. Choose its clues, then test it on Mars and Neptune.

features.text: Closer to the Sun than the asteroid belt

locks.hint: Earth has a moon too. Which clue really separates the inner four from the outer four?
locks.learn: 'Has moons' can't separate the groups, because Earth and Mars have moons. Clues that match how the groups are defined (position, or ring systems) work.

locks.title: Check NOVA's sky claim
locks.intro: NOVA explains the daytime sky. Is it right? Decide and pick the fact that settles it.
locks.claim: The stars disappear during the day.
evidence: Stars are in the sky in the daytime too, but the bright sunlight makes them invisible.
The pole star doesn't seem to move.
locks.hint: Not seeing something isn't the same as it not being there.
locks.learn: An AI that only learns from what it 'sees' can confuse 'can't see' with 'isn't there'. Knowing the reason (sunlight) corrects it.

locks.title: Predict the full moon
locks.intro: NOVA recorded the Moon's shape after a full moon.
locks.question: About how many days after the last full moon will the next full moon be?
locks.hint: The pattern repeats: full, half, new, half, then ...?
locks.learn: The Moon's phases repeat about every 29.5 days, so a pattern found in the data lets NOVA predict the next full moon. Patterns that come from regular motion are very predictable.

locks.title: Fix NOVA's sky catalogue
locks.intro: NOVA has a catalogue of objects in the solar system. Tick the entries that are wrong.

rows.label: Grows a long, glowing tail near the Sun
A 'shooting star' that burns up in the air
An artificial satellite
rows.why: the Moon is a natural satellite

rows.label: Never reaches the Earth
rows.why: meteorites are the pieces that do reach the Earth

locks.hint: Which satellites are made by people? What makes a meteorite different from a meteor?
locks.learn: Words that look alike (meteor, meteorite) are easy to mix up when labelling. Careful labels help AI and people alike.
